params.body: ## Why The hero image on the KUBO CyberSec page (the `sudo ./learn` keycap sticker) has an alt text, but it spells the prompt on the key as a literal `>_`. A screen reader reads that aloud as "greater than, underscore", which tells a blind visitor nothing about the picture. The raw `>` inside the `alt` attribute is valid HTML, but tag scanners that read `` up to the first `>` cut the tag off there and report the image as having no alt text. That is how /communities/cybersec/ and /nl/communities/cybersec/ came out as the only two images on the site without alt text. The FR page passed only because its alt text has an apostrophe before the `>`. ## What In `src/components/CyberSecPage.astro`, the `stickerAlt` text in all three languages now names the prompt instead of spelling it: - EN: "... with a coral command-line prompt symbol below it, ..." - NL: "... daaronder een koraalrood teken van een opdrachtprompt, ..." - FR: "... en dessous un symbole d'invite de commande corail, ..." The rest of each description is unchanged. The small sticker on the /communities cards keeps `alt=""`: it is decorative next to a card that already names the community. ## Checked - Crawled all 40 URLs in the live sitemap: 542 `` tags, every one with an `alt` attribute. The two flagged images are the CyberSec sticker on the EN and NL pages. Live matches `main` for these images. - `npm ci`, `npm test` (4 files, 25 tests pass), `npm run build` (42 pages), `npm run check:built` (passes). - Ran the same "img up to the first `>`, then look for `alt=`" check over the built `dist/` pages: no images flagged.
params.title: CyberSec sticker alt text: describe the prompt instead of spelling >_
